guide.summary: OAuth is documented for OpenProject: register an OAuth application, run the authorization code flow, then call GET /api/v3/work_packages with a bearer token. The api_v3 scope covers the standard API. Results are limited to work packages the connected user can view in each project. Each customer instance needs its own OAuth application, registered by that instance's administrator. Tests are untested until executed. Customer-rollout review requirements are unknown.

findings.title: OAuth2 authorization code flow is documented
findings.detail: OpenProject documents its OAuth2 auth and token endpoints and an authorization code flow for obtaining an access token.

evidence.quote: OAuth endpoints The authentication endpoints of OpenProject OAuth2 server are:
Auth URL: https://example.com/oauth/authorize Access Token URL: https://example.com/oauth/token

https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.

findings.title: Request the api_v3 scope for the standard API
findings.detail: Select api_v3 when registering the application. If no scope is checked, api_v3 is assumed. It is the standard OpenProject API scope.

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.

findings.title: Each customer instance needs its own OAuth application
findings.detail: The instance administrator creates the application (name, redirect URL, scopes) and notes the Client ID and secret. Applications are per instance.

evidence.quote: Enter the Name of your OAuth application.
Define a Redirect URL where users are redirected to after having authorized OAuth2 access in OpenProject. This URL is provided by your client application. In the case of locally running
Press Create to add your OAuth application.
Tip Don’t forget to note down your Client ID and your Client secret in a safe space. You will need them later.

findings.title: Connected user needs view permission on work packages
findings.detail: The list returns only work packages the user is allowed to view. Test accounts need the view_work_packages permission in at least one project, and a denied record returns not-found rather than forbidden.

evidence.quote: All work packages a user is allowed a permission in WorkPackage.allowed_to(user, permission) WorkPackage.allowed_to(User.current, :view_work_packages)
We return 404 instead of 403 to not reveal the existence of a record.
"errorIdentifier" : "urn:openproject-org:api:v3:errors:MissingPermission" ,

steps.title: Implement authorization redirect and code-to-token exchange
steps.detail: Build the authorization redirect, the callback that receives the code, and the token exchange using the documented token request. Do not run the authorization flow in this step.
steps.doneWhen: Code implements the authorize redirect, callback handling, and token exchange against the test instance base URL.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.

steps.detail: Using a test account on the test instance, complete consent in the browser and exchange the returned code for an access token. Record the expiry.
steps.doneWhen: The callback receives a code and the token exchange returns an access_token with expires_in.

steps.title: Test first page of work package titles (action)
steps.detail: Call the work package list with a small page size using the test user's bearer token. Expected: a HAL collection with _embedded elements that include subject titles and paging fields. Boundary check: confirm only this GET is sent, the response contains only work packages visible to that test user, and the app request log shows no PATCH, POST, or DELETE.
steps.doneWhen: The first page returns work package titles and the request log shows only GET calls.

evidence.quote: get /api/v3/work_packages Returns a collection of work packages.
pageSize integer optional query
Number of elements to display per page.
<Token> with the bearer token you obtained above.
--header 'Authorization: Bearer <Token>' `

fields: Access token from the test authorization step

steps.title: Test second page of work package titles (action, pagination)
steps.detail: Request the next page with offset=2 and the same page size. Expected: different elements from the first page and consistent paging metadata. Boundary check: confirm the request is GET only and no work package changed.
steps.doneWhen: Page 2 returns work package titles that differ from page 1, and the request log shows only GET calls.

evidence.quote: Parameters offset integer optional query
Page number inside the requested collection.
pageSize integer optional query
Number of elements to display per page.
